children: , the consumer-technology and computing giant, pushed deeper into enterprise AI with new Mac Mini and Mac Studio systems designed to run powerful models locally instead of constantly sending workloads to the cloud. Shares gained approximately 0.8% to $341.53 Tuesday.

The pitch is simple: buy the computing power once and keep more AI workloads inside the building. High-end configurations can approach $20,000, while Apple demonstrated four Mac Studios working together to run a trillion-parameter model from a single wall outlet. Its RDMA-over-Thunderbolt technology links the machines into a low-latency cluster, giving businesses another route to private AI infrastructure. The challenge is distribution. Reuters cited IDC estimates showing Apple controls just 4.6% of enterprise computers, compared with 91.3% for Windows-based systems.

That makes the economics more interesting than the hardware demonstration itself. Companies running AI models heavily enough could eventually prefer upfront equipment costs over an endless stream of cloud-token bills, while local processing adds privacy and more predictable spending. But investors are already paying a premium for that opportunity: the valuation snapshot puts Apple at $341.53 versus a GF Value of $286.67, meaning the shares trade 19.14% above GF Value. Apple now has to turn a clever private-AI architecture into meaningful enterprise adoption before that premium gets easier to justify.

title: Apple Gains as $20,000 Macs Challenge Metered AI
